title: What Is the Average Engineer Salary in Australia? A Full Guide to Hourly, Annual, Tax and Super
description: Find the average engineer salary in Australia using ABS data and Fair Work rates. Learn how to convert hourly to annual, plus tax and super calculations.

faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then by 52. For a standard full‑time role, assume 38 hours per week. For example, $50 per hour × 38 hours × 52 weeks = $98,800 per year. This calculation assumes the same rate every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. faqs.q: What is the average engineer salary in Australia?
faqs.a: The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports that professionals (a category that includes engineers) earned average weekly total cash earnings of $2,049.60 in May 2025. That works out to roughly $106,579 per year for a 38‑hour week. However, engineer salaries vary widely by industry, experience, and location. faqs.q: How is superannuation paid on top of my salary?

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Average Engineer Salary in Australia

If you’re searching for the **average engineer salary in Australia**, you’ve come to the right place. Engineers are among the highest‑paid professionals in the country, but actual earnings depend on your specialisation, experience, and whether you work full‑time, part‑time, or on a casual basis. This guide uses the latest data from the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS), the Fair Work Ombudsman, and the Fair Work Commission to give you a clear picture of what engineers earn and how to convert an hourly rate to an annual figure.

## How to Convert Hourly Pay to Annual Salary

The basic formula is simple:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

Most full‑time roles in Australia are based on a 38‑hour week. If you’re paid by the hour, multiply your rate by 38 and then by 52 to get your yearly income before tax and super. For example, an engineer earning $60 per hour would have:

$60 × 38 × 52 = $118,560 per year

If you work part‑time or casual, adjust the hours accordingly. The [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool on this site does the maths for you.

### Fortnightly Pay

Many employers pay fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross pay, simply multiply your weekly pay by 2. Using the example above:

Weekly pay = $60 × 38 = $2,280
Fortnightly pay = $2,280 × 2 = $4,560

This can help you budget if you’re paid on a fortnightly cycle.

## What the Data Says About Engineer Salaries

The ABS collects detailed earnings data every year. In its May 2025 release, the average weekly total cash earnings for all employees was $1,611.10, but for professionals (the occupational group that includes engineers) it was $2,049.60. That translates to roughly $106,579 per year for a 38‑hour week. However, this figure includes part‑time workers. For full‑time adult employees, the ABS reported average weekly ordinary time earnings of $2,083.70 in May 2026 (from our on‑site reference), which is about $108,352 per year.

### Engineers vs Other Professionals

Engineers often earn more than the professional average. The ABS data shows that managers (a category that includes senior engineers) earned an average of $2,800.90 per week, while technicians and trades workers earned $1,756.90. Engineers typically fall between these groups. For a more precise estimate, check the [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page for industry‑specific figures.

## Minimum Wages and Award Rates

Not all engineers are covered by awards, but it’s important to know the legal minimums. From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. Award minimum wages increased by 4.75% from that date. For casual employees, a 25% loading applies, making the casual minimum $33.05 per hour. Most engineers earn well above these rates, but if you’re starting out or working in a lower‑paid engineering role, your award may set a higher minimum.

### Casual Loading

If you work as a casual engineer, your employer must pay a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate. This compensates for not receiving paid leave. When using our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) calculator, enter your base rate (without loading) and check the casual box – the tool will add the 25% automatically.

## Tax and Super Considerations

Once you know your annual gross salary, you can estimate your take‑home pay. For the 2026–27 financial year, the resident tax rates are:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% on the excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: 30% on the excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: 37% on the excess over $135,000
- $190,001+: 45% on the excess over $190,000

Plus a Medicare levy of 2% (with possible reductions for low incomes). Use our [take‑home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator for a personalised estimate.

### Superannuation Guarantee

Super is paid on top of your salary. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee rate is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to a maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For an engineer earning $120,000, that means an extra $14,400 contributed to super each year. This amount is not part of your take‑home pay but is a valuable retirement benefit. See [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) for more details.

## Putting It All Together

To find the **average engineer salary in Australia**, start with the ABS data: professionals averaged about $2,050 per week in May 2025. But your actual pay depends on your role, industry, and whether you’re full‑time or casual. Use the formula hourly × 38 × 52 to convert your rate to annual, and don’t forget to add super on top. For award‑covered engineers, check the relevant [pay guides](/blog) from the Fair Work Ombudsman. And always remember that the figures here are estimates – your individual circumstances may differ.
